transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, two years ago I took over running my own boutique dry cleaning shop, but lately I've been really struggling to keep things organized. I keep misplacing order tickets, receipts, and other important items around the shop, and the resulting mix-ups are starting to hurt my business.

Have you had problems with organization, losing things, or staying focused since childhood or school, or did these difficulties start only after taking over the shop? Were there any major stresses or life changes around the time they began?

Taking over the shop two years ago was a massive transition that really brought these issues to a head, but I've actually struggled with milder versions of this since childhood. Back in elementary school, my teachers would always write on my report cards that I was constantly chatting, getting out of my seat, and losing my worksheets or homework. It just became much harder to manage once I had to run the whole business myself.
Besides at the shop, do these attention or organization problems also affect other parts of your life, like at home, with bills, appointments, or relationships? Can you give one or two examples?

Yes, it definitely spills over into my home life and church commitments. My husband complains that I'm too drained and distracted to really be present, and I constantly zone out when he's talking to me about things at home, forcing me to ask him to repeat himself.

Do these attention and organization problems happen almost every day and in most situations, even when you’re not especially stressed or overwhelmed? Or do they mainly flare up only during high-stress periods like running the shop?

They definitely happen almost every day, even when things are relatively quiet and I'm not feeling super stressed. The pressure of running the shop has just made the consequences a lot worse, but the basic struggle with zoning out and losing things is always there.
Do these attention and organization problems cause major problems in daily life, like missed deadlines, unpaid bills, accidents, or repeated mistakes at work? What is the biggest example recently?

Yes, they absolutely cause major problems, like a recent mix-up with a wedding gown order that left a customer furious, and my accountant pointing out too many avoidable administrative tangles. I'm forced to stay late several nights a week to fix these mistakes, which leaves me too drained and distracted to be present with my husband or keep up with my church commitments.
Besides the inattention and disorganization, do you also often feel restless or fidgety, talk excessively, interrupt others, or act before thinking? Were those behaviors present since childhood too?

Yes, I absolutely do. I get very restless and pop up from my seat during church or when doing computer work, and I often talk too much, interrupt others, or get extremely impatient waiting in lines. My elementary school teachers actually noted this back then too, constantly writing on my report cards that I was always chatting and getting out of my seat.
